The offer-level candidates combine an offer-level promotional connection with existence of a non-discount gift component. If the promotional connection necessarily covers that component, the aggregation may be justified. If a mixed offer includes unrelated components, the formulas may impose an unsupported restriction by catching a gift without establishing its own promotional connection. The necessary same-component relationship is not explicit in the existential facts.

Unit db43e253bea18.u0.2 defines distributors as intermediaries distributing SFC-authorised funds. Broad distributor and investment-product wording in some candidate facts must retain that circular scope. The quoted paragraph 3.11 may support a broader assessment, but its independent scope cannot be established from an unavailable external text.

Unit db43e253bea18.u12.2646 says guaranteed returns and incentives may be considered gifts. Neither automatic gift classification nor automatic exemption follows. Gift classification remains supplied judgment; the formulas do not implement that judgment. The fee-or-charge exception concerns the assessed component and does not exempt a distinct non-discount gift elsewhere in the offer.

The source makes offering the operative act, so completed payment or receipt is not required by the quoted restriction. However, the categorical independence of funding and fulfilment is not expressly resolved for every third-party arrangement. Preserve offer attribution as an unresolved factual and interpretive issue rather than treating the candidate's description as source-established law.

It supplies no permission to use misleading advertisements, imply deposit equivalence, or breach the separate structured-product provisions.
